actions.justification: Mandatory per KDIGO guidelines before contrast exposure. CKD stage 4 patient is at high risk for contrast-associated AKI; hydration status directly affects renal protection strategy.
Mandatory per KDIGO guidelines. Must know baseline eGFR before administering contrast in this CKD stage 4 patient to assess CA-AKI risk and guide decisions about contrast administration.
Mandatory per KDIGO guidelines. Patient has multiple risk factors (CKD stage 4, diabetes, hypertension) that must be formally reviewed before contrast exposure to stratify CA-AKI risk.

Patient has type 2 diabetes — must check if metformin is being taken, as it must be held before and 48h after iodinated contrast to prevent lactic acidosis if contrast-induced AKI occurs. Also review other nephrotoxins (NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors) given CKD stage 4.

Patient has CKD stage 4 with elevated BP; calculating the maximum safe contrast volume based on eGFR helps minimize nephrotoxic risk per KDIGO CA-AKI guidelines before proceeding with contrast CT for suspected AAA.
Given CKD stage 4, consider whether non-contrast CT or ultrasound could adequately evaluate for AAA, potentially avoiding contrast exposure entirely and preserving residual renal function.
Patient has CKD stage 4 — avoid NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, and other nephrotoxins prior to contrast exposure to minimize CA-AKI risk per KDIGO guidelines.
Monitoring urine output is essential in CKD stage 4 patients before contrast administration to assess baseline renal perfusion and hydration status.
CKD stage 4 with planned contrast CT for suspected AAA warrants nephrology input to guide risk stratification, pre-hydration strategy, and post-contrast monitoring per KDIGO CA-AKI guidelines.

Patient has CKD stage 4 and is being prepared for contrast CT. Discontinuing nephrotoxic agents (including NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, etc.) before contrast exposure reduces the additive risk of contrast-associated AKI per KDIGO guidelines.

Patient has CKD stage 4 and diabetes type 2. Metformin must be held before iodinated contrast and for 48h after per KDIGO guidelines to prevent metformin-associated lactic acidosis in the setting of contrast-induced AKI. Other renally-dosed medications should also be reviewed.

Document the baseline eGFR assessment already completed to ensure contrast administration decision is appropriately recorded per KDIGO contrast-AKI risk assessment protocol, and to establish baseline for post-contrast renal function trending.

Patient has type 2 diabetes and is likely on metformin. Per KDIGO guidelines, metformin must be held before iodinated contrast and for 48h after to prevent metformin accumulation in the event of contrast-induced AKI.
IV hydration with isotonic crystalloid is a cornerstone of CA-AKI prevention per KDIGO guidelines, especially in high-risk patients with CKD stage 4.
Serial vital sign monitoring is indicated to track hemodynamic status and detect any changes in this high-risk patient prior to contrast administration.
Patient has CKD stage 4; all nephrotoxic medications must be held to minimize risk of contrast-associated AKI per KDIGO guidelines.

Patient has type 2 diabetes and CKD stage 4 (eGFR likely <45 mL/min/1.73m²). Metformin must be held before contrast and for 48h after iodinated contrast administration to prevent lactic acidosis per KDIGO guidelines.
Pre-emptive planning for post-contrast IV hydration is indicated for this high-risk CKD stage 4 patient to mitigate contrast-associated AKI per KDIGO guidelines.

Patient has CKD stage 4 with elevated BP and is about to receive contrast. Pre-contrast IV hydration (isotonic crystalloid) is a key KDIGO recommendation to mitigate contrast-associated AKI risk, even though post-contrast hydration is already done — ensuring adequate hydration before contrast administration is critical.
Monitoring urine output in a CKD stage 4 patient receiving contrast is essential per KDIGO guidelines to detect early signs of contrast-associated AKI and guide ongoing fluid management.
KDIGO guidelines recommend monitoring serum creatinine at 48-72 hours post-contrast in high-risk patients (CKD stage 4) to detect contrast-associated AKI in a timely manner.
Monitor serum creatinine at 48 hours post-contrast per KDIGO guidelines to detect contrast-associated AKI in this high-risk CKD stage 4 patient.
Nephrology consultation is warranted given CKD stage 4 with contrast exposure risk; nephrology can guide further management including potential RRT if AKI develops.
Ongoing optimization of fluid status is critical in this CKD stage 4 patient post-contrast to minimize AKI risk and support renal perfusion.
Patient with CKD stage 4 who received contrast requires serial creatinine monitoring per KDIGO guidelines to detect contrast-associated AKI. SCr should be checked at 48-72h post-contrast.
KDIGO guidelines recommend checking SCr at 48-72h post-contrast exposure in high-risk patients (CKD stage 4). This is a mandatory follow-up to detect delayed contrast-associated AKI.
Patient with CKD stage 4 and hypertension may require ongoing IV hydration post-contrast to maintain renal perfusion and mitigate contrast-associated AKI risk per KDIGO guidelines.
Document current eGFR status given CKD stage 4 - important for tracking renal function trajectory after contrast exposure for suspected AAA workup.
Bedside ultrasound can assess for AAA without contrast, which is important given CKD stage 4 and contrast-associated AKI risk. This may serve as an alternative or complementary imaging to CT.
Patient has CKD stage 4 and if contrast CT is ultimately needed, KDIGO guidelines recommend considering dialysis scheduling post-contrast. Planning ahead given CKD status is appropriate.
Monitor renal function (BMP includes creatinine/BUN) post-contrast in CKD stage 4 patient; essential for tracking contrast-associated AKI development given high risk profile.
Baseline CBC for suspected AAA workup to assess hemoglobin/hematocrit in case of occult bleeding and overall hematologic status.
Patient has hypertension and diabetes with elevated BP (165/92); ECG helps evaluate for cardiac comorbidities and baseline cardiac status before procedural intervention.

Serial creatinine monitoring is essential per KDIGO guidelines for CKD Stage 4 patients receiving contrast. Baseline creatinine tracking and post-contrast trending (48-72h) is critical to detect contrast-associated AKI early.
Coagulation studies are important for a patient with suspected AAA who may require urgent surgical or endovascular intervention. CKD can also affect platelet function and coagulation.

Per KDIGO guidelines, CKD Stage 4 patients receiving iodinated contrast should be assessed for post-contrast renal replacement therapy scheduling, particularly given significantly reduced renal reserve and risk of contrast-associated AKI.
